'''Lucy Jane Carpenter''' (born 21 October 1969) is a British chemist who is a [[professor]] of [[physical chemistry]] at the [[University of York]].  She was one of the founding scientists and director of the Cape Verde Atmospheric Observatory (CVAO), established on [[São Vicente, Cape Verde|São Vicente]] in 2006 and now a key global monitoring site.<ref name=rs>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160301191455/https://royalsociety.org/people/lucy-carpenter-100000006/|archive-date=2016-03-01|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/lucy-carpenter-100000006/|author=Anon|year=2015|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|website=royalsociety.org|title=Professor Lucy Carpenter|location=London}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|“All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]].” --{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111170346/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/|title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies|date=2016-11-11}}}}</ref><ref name=epmc>{{EuropePMC|ORCID=0000-0002-6257-3950}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.york.ac.uk/chemistry/staff/academic/a-c/lcarpenter/|website=york.ac.uk|title=Professor Lucy Carpenter: Atmospheric Chemistry}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.york.ac.uk/research/athena-swan/benefits/lucy-carpenter/|title=Athena Swan, Lucy Carpenter|website=york.ac.uk|access-date=2018-02-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190506014514/https://www.york.ac.uk/research/athena-swan/benefits/lucy-carpenter/|archive-date=2019-05-06|url-status=dead}}</ref> Her work has helped to transform understanding of how oceans shape the air above them.

==Education==
Carpenter graduated with a BSc in chemistry from the [[University of Bristol]] in 1991<ref name=rs/> followed by a [[PhD]] in [[atmospheric chemistry]] at the [[University of East Anglia]] supervised by Stuart Penkett<ref name=rs/> and awarded in 1996.<ref name=PhD-317982>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of East Anglia|url=http://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/9551394?style=html|title=Measurements of peroxy radicals in clean and polluted atmospheres|first= Lucy Jane|last=Carpenter|date=1996|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.317982}}|website=copac.jisc.ac.uk|oclc=53665545}}</ref>

==Research and career==
Her group studies the complex interaction between the oceans and the atmosphere, in particular the chemistry of reactive [[halogen]]s, [[organic carbon]], and [[reactive nitrogen]].<ref name=rs/><ref name=googlescholar>{{Google scholar id}}</ref>  Her work on oceanic and atmospheric halogens has established this chemistry as an important component of [[tropospheric ozone]] cycling and makes use of [[gas chromatography–mass spectrometry]] (GCMS).<ref name="Simpsonvon Glasow2007">{{cite journal|last1=Simpson|first1=W. C.|title=Extensive halogen-mediated ozone destruction over the tropical Atlantic Ocean|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|pmid= 18580948 |volume=453|issue=7199|year=2008|pages=1232–1235|issn=0028-0836|doi=10.1038/nature07035|bibcode=2008Natur.453.1232R|s2cid=4430074}}</ref>

She helped establish the Cape Verde Atmospheric Observatory, one of a few dozen [[World Meteorological Organization]] (WMO) [[Global Atmosphere Watch]] (GAW) stations worldwide which monitor climate and air quality gases over long time scales, and was a lead chapter author of the WMO/[[United Nations Environment Programme]] (UNEP) 2014 scientific assessment of [[ozone depletion]].<ref name=rs/>

Carpenter is one of the co-chairs of the Scientific Assessment Panel<ref>{{Cite web |title=SAP Members {{!}} Ozone Secretariat |url=https://ozone.unep.org/science/assessment/sap/sap-members |access-date=2026-03-25 |website=ozone.unep.org}}</ref> for the [[Montreal Protocol]] and presented at the 37th Meeting of the Parties (MOP37) in [[Nairobi]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=York |first=University of |title=Professor Carpenter Addresses Montreal Protocol Meeting on the Scientific Evidence of Ozone-Depleting Substances and Climate Gases |url=https://www.york.ac.uk/chemistry/about/news/2025/montreal-protocol-meeting/ |access-date=2026-03-25 |website=University of York |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In March 2026, Carpenter was featured on [[The Life Scientific]] to speak about the impact of oceans on [[ozone]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=BBC Radio 4 - The Life Scientific, Lucy Carpenter on how our oceans are destroying ozone |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m002t18r |access-date=2026-11-05 |website=BBC |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Carpenter has received several awards for her research. She received a [[Philip Leverhulme Prize]] in 'Earth Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences' in 2006, and was given the [[Rosalind Franklin Award]] from the [[Royal Society]] in 2015 for "her scientific achievement, her suitability as a role model and her project proposal to promote women in [[Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics|STEM]]".<ref name=ros>{{cite web|last=Carpenter|first=Lucy|year=2015|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bhOX8tY5lSE|website=youtube.com|title = What on Earth is happening to our atmosphere? Rosalind Franklin Award Lecture}}</ref> She received the [[Tilden Prize]] in 2017.<ref name=frs/> In 2019, Carpenter was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS).<ref name=frs>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/lucy-carpenter-14083/|title=Professor Lucy Carpenter FRS |publisher=Royal Society |date=2019|author=Anon|website=royalsociety.org |access-date=2019-04-17}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|“All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]].” --{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111170346/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/|title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies|date=2016-11-11}}}}</ref> She was awarded the 2024 [[Vilhelm Bjerknes Medal]] "for establishing a critical link between the production of trace gases in and over the oceans, atmospheric chemistry, and climate change".<ref name="egu2024">{{cite web |title=Lucy Carpenter : Vilhelm Bjerknes Medal 2023 |url=https://www.egu.eu/awards-medals/vilhelm-bjerknes/2024/lucy-carpenter/ |website=European Geosciences Union |access-date=3 April 2024}}</ref>

Carpenter was appointed [[Member of the Order of the British Empire]] (MBE) in the [[2022 New Year Honours]] for services to atmospheric chemistry.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=63571|supp=y|page=N17|date=1 January 2022}}</ref>
